$comment: Status per area: ported | partial | planned | wont-port | unknown. Notes and evidence are optional; evidence is a URL. Assessed against the repository, not docs claims: authored test suites, goldens captured from Pi 1.1.0, compatibility/*.v1.1.0 inventories and overlays, and compatibility/sync-1.1.0-applicability.json. deviations lists the differences that remain, intentional ones first.

promises.label: Behavioral parity
promises.blurb: Does PiSharp do what Pi does? Same prompts, tools, ordering and results for the same inputs.

rows.notes: Steering and follow-up queues with both drain modes, parallel tool batches, abort and automatic retry. turn_end drafts and message_end replacements apply inside the running loop, as in Pi.

rows.area: Built-in tools: read, write, edit, bash, grep, find, ls
rows.notes: Pi's declarations, arguments and errors. read returns images, decoded and resized with SkiaSharp. bash finds its shell as Pi does, with shellCommandPrefix and user_bash interception; without a shell it stays registered and each command fails with Pi's message, and a shell that can't start reports Node's spawn error. grep and find use rg and fd, downloaded on first use.

All 10 of Pi's chat APIs, including Bedrock, Codex and Copilot, all 42 provider catalogs and the llama.cpp router provider, each with a live route and /login. OpenAI Codex tries a WebSocket first and compresses server-sent-event requests with zstd, as Pi does. --model patterns, --models, --list-models (with extension providers), models.json and the startup catalog refresh work. Azure resource names are taken as Pi takes them (decision 14). Differences: the websocketConnectTimeoutMs setting isn't read (the WebSocket gets 15 seconds), and models.json validation errors only approximate TypeBox's messages.

OpenAI decisions (with image input), TypeSafe and Cloudflare system-one, llama.cpp decision models and log-probability classification, and OpenRouter images. Reachable from codemode, native extensions and TypeScript extensions, both of which can also register their own classifier and image providers.

Plain pisharp takes every flag in Pi's args.ts, with -p, --mode json|rpc, @file arguments and the install, remove, update, list, config, auth and mcp commands. -e loads packages with their skills, prompts and themes, and -e builtin:<name> a built-in extension; pisharp config switches the built-ins. Print mode recovers from a context overflow through auto-compaction and exits 0, as Pi does. pisharp update can't update PiSharp itself.

Sessions in ~/.pi/agent/sessions, --continue, --resume, --session, --session-id, --fork, --session-dir and --no-session, /name, /session, /fork, /clone, /tree, /resume, HTML export and /share. Session files are compared with files Pi 1.1.0 wrote for the same scripts.

Manual and automatic compaction and branch summaries, with Pi's summary retries, events and error texts. Automatic compaction is on by default in every mode and reads the compaction settings, including per-model overrides.

All 24 of Pi's built-in commands, with the same names, descriptions and arguments, plus /mcp and /llama from the built-in extensions. /bug builds Pi's local report and opens a prefilled PiSharp GitHub issue instead of uploading to Pi's developers.

rows.area: Skills, prompt templates and context files
rows.notes: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md from the agent folder and every parent folder, SYSTEM.md and APPEND_SYSTEM.md, and skills, prompts and themes discovered from Pi's folders, settings, packages and -e, behind project trust.

Pi's interactive mode on Windows, Linux and macOS: fullscreen and regular modes, every /settings item, the system, dark and light themes and custom theme files, keybindings.json, inline images, Mermaid and highlight.js highlighting. The footer's cost, tokens and context follow the session after every turn. On X11, pasting reads the clipboard through libxcb when xclip and xsel are missing, as Pi's helper does.

Stdio and HTTP servers, ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json and the trusted project .pi/mcp.json, OAuth with refresh locks, all exposure modes, resource tools, the 10-second wait for direct servers, the mcp_servers prompt section, /mcp in every mode and pisharp mcp. MCP is a built-in extension that can be turned off. Difference: /reload keeps the servers connected and doesn't re-read mcp.json unless the mcp, codemode or tool-search built-ins changed; Pi reconnects on every reload.
Pi's BM25 search, always registered and switched off as in Pi. It waits for background servers, and its prompt snippet is rendered.

Pi's prelude, script API, store, models bridge and limits, on the Jint engine. Codemode MCP servers connect. Intentional: each script runs in its own worker process (about 100 to 300 ms to start), its deadline starts when the script starts, and memory and recursion overruns end the script instead of throwing.

promises.label: Session & RPC compatibility
promises.blurb: Can PiSharp read and write the same files and speak the same protocol, so tools built for Pi keep working?

rows.notes: Reads JSONL v3 session trees and keeps unknown entries and fields. Lone surrogates are kept as JSON.parse keeps them. Records may nest 1,000 levels; V8 itself stops writing at about 1,700.
Every line is the bytes JSON.stringify writes, in Pi's key order. Compared entry by entry with session files captured from Pi 1.1.0.
Pi's own v1 and v2 migration on open, and session copy and session migrate, which leave the original file unchanged.

Every event Pi sends, including entry_appended, thinking_level_changed, extension_error, auto_retry_* and summarization_retry_*. agent_end carries willRetry, and agent_settled arrives before the response to the command that started the run.

All 33 Pi v1.1.0 RPC commands. A failed command answers with the error's message, thinking levels are clamped to the model, and the setters save the global settings.json, as in Pi. Under pisharp --mode rpc, bash runs in your shell with no extra options. Difference: get_session_stats fails on non-finite usage, where Pi reports null.
select, confirm, input, editor, notify, setStatus, setWidget, setTitle and set_editor_text requests, and their responses.

Each line is read and written as rpc-mode.ts does, with lone surrogates kept and lines up to JavaScript's string limit. A line nested deeper than 1,000 levels is answered as a parse failure and the stream goes on. SIGTERM and SIGHUP shut down as in Pi.
settings.json, auth.json, models.json, mcp.json, mcp-auth.json, keybindings.json and trust.json in ~/.pi/agent (or PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR), and the project .pi folder. !command values run, as in Pi.

promises.label: Extension compatibility
promises.blurb: Do Pi's TypeScript extensions and packages run unchanged? PiSharp runs them in Node with Pi's own npm packages, installed and verified on first use. Native C# extensions load from the same folders. The extension suite runs in the release pipeline with Node 22.

rows.notes: Discovered from ~/.pi/agent/extensions, .pi/extensions (after project trust), settings, packages and -e, as in Pi. Pi's built-in extensions (mcp, llama.cpp, codemode, tool-search) can be turned off or replaced. Needs Node.js 22.13 or later; Pi asks for 22.19.

pi-coding-agent, pi-ai, pi-tui and pi-agent-core 1.1.0 are installed with your npm, checked against the registry's integrity, and loaded through Pi's jiti. Offline, or without npm, extensions fall back to built-in copies with a warning.
Every member: tools, commands, shortcuts, flags, providers (chat, classifier and image), virtual models, MCP servers, ctx.ui.setTheme and the event bus.
Every v1.1.0 extension event reaches TypeScript handlers. sendMessage with triggerTurn starts its turn at once, inside a command or from a timer, as in Pi.
ctx.ui dialogs, widgets and custom components, registerMessageRenderer and registerToolRenderer, in the terminal UI and over RPC.
pisharp install, remove, update, list and config for npm, git and local sources, global or project (-l), with Pi's trust rules.

A folder with a pisharp-extension.json loads from the same places as Pi extensions, without Node, and shares the session and command list with TypeScript extensions. All 41 v1.1.0 events reach native handlers, and native extensions can register classifier and image providers. Difference: a C# extension that registers codemode, tool_search or /mcp doesn't replace the built-in one; only TypeScript extensions do.

items.title: No telemetry
items.notes: PiSharp doesn't report installs to Pi's servers. PI_TELEMETRY and enableInstallTelemetry are accepted and ignored.

items.title: Startup header
items.notes: The header says PiSharp with PiSharp's own version (for example v1.1.0.3), where Pi shows its package version.

items.title: User agents
items.notes: Requests to Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Mistral, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and OpenRouter images send a PiSharp user agent where Pi's SDKs send their own.

items.title: Codemode worker
items.notes: Each script runs in its own worker process, so one script can't take PiSharp down. That costs about 100 to 300 ms per script. The deadline starts when the script starts running, not when the worker launches.

items.title: Jint limits
items.notes: Codemode runs on Jint, not QuickJS. Memory and recursion overruns end the script instead of throwing a catchable error, and the engine's own error messages differ.

items.title: /bug opens a GitHub issue
items.notes: /bug builds Pi's report and zip but never uploads them to Pi's developers. It opens a prefilled issue at github.com/jkelly/PiSharp for you to attach the zip to.

items.title: Version check on NuGet
items.notes: The update check looks up the latest PiSharp.Cli on NuGet and suggests dotnet tool update -g PiSharp.Cli. It never asks pi.dev.

items.title: No self-update
items.notes: pisharp update updates packages and catalogs. Update PiSharp itself with dotnet tool update -g PiSharp.Cli.

deviations.title: Still open
deviations.blurb: Differences that remain to be fixed or decided.

items.title: /reload and MCP
items.notes: /reload keeps MCP servers connected, and doesn't re-read mcp.json, unless the mcp, codemode or tool-search built-ins changed. Pi reconnects every server on every reload.

items.title: /reload diagnostics
items.notes: After /reload, only extension load errors are shown. Pi also shows built-in replacement warnings, unknown built-in names, package resolution problems and skill, prompt and theme conflicts.

items.title: Built-in replacement
items.notes: A built-in extension yields only to a TypeScript extension that registers codemode, tool_search or /mcp. A C# extension that registers one doesn't replace the built-in.

items.title: JSON depth 1,000
items.notes: Session records, RPC input and other JSON values hold 1,000 levels of nesting. Pi's JSON.parse has no limit, though V8's JSON.stringify gives up at about 1,700 levels, so Pi can't store deeper values either.

items.title: Explicit session verbs
items.notes: The pisharp session … and rpc verbs keep their byte bounds (64 MiB session lines and files, 32 MiB RPC records, 8 MiB tool results) and refuse lone surrogates. The Pi command line has neither limit. Provider request bodies stay limited to 64 MiB, and single request entries to 16 MiB, everywhere.

items.title: Non-finite usage
items.notes: get_session_stats fails when a session holds non-finite usage numbers, where Pi reports null.

items.title: models.json errors
items.notes: models.json validation errors use TypeBox's wording but not its full list: a failed union reports only "must match a schema in anyOf".

items.title: WebSocket connect timeout
items.notes: The websocketConnectTimeoutMs setting isn't read. The Codex WebSocket always gets 15 seconds to open, Pi's default.

items.title: Azure resource names
items.notes: Any resource name is taken as Pi takes it (decision 14). A name that leaves credentials, a fragment or a query in the URL, or a host .NET can't hold (such as one with $ or an empty label), is refused when the session starts; Pi fails only when it sends the request.

phases.title: Freeze the compatibility target
phases.notes: Pinned to Pi v1.1.0, with the command, RPC and event inventories refreshed. Release profiles (P1-04) are still open.

phases.title: Provider layer
phases.notes: All 10 of Pi's chat APIs, 42 provider catalogs, the llama.cpp router, logins, classifiers and images, and the Codex WebSocket transport with zstd.

phases.title: Agent loop and tools
phases.notes: Loop, all built-in tools with images, codemode and tool_search.

phases.title: Sessions
phases.notes: Pi's session folder and format, byte for byte, with branching, compaction, export and sharing.

phases.title: Headless RPC, then terminal UI
phases.notes: Pi's command line, print, JSON and RPC modes, and the interactive UI with every slash command.

phases.title: Native extension SDK
phases.notes: C# extensions load from Pi's extension folders. All 41 events reach native handlers, and native extensions register classifier and image providers.

phases.title: Optional Node bridge
phases.notes: Runs any Pi extension and package on Pi's own npm packages.

phases.title: Hardening and packaging
phases.notes: The release pipeline runs 17 offline suites on Linux, including the extension suite with Node. Platform and security qualification are open.

phases.title: 1.1.0.x gap releases
phases.notes: tool_search shipped in 1.1.0.1 and the rest of Pi v1.1.0 in 1.1.0.2. 1.1.0.3 fixes issue #5 and closes most of the differences 1.1.0.2 left open; 1.1.0.5 names PiSharp in the startup header and fixes lone surrogates in compaction estimates.
